name: WayriCAD Quick PI
description: DC PI, AC/SMPS copper losses, explicit rail transients and electrothermal coupling.
description_full: Solve DC voltage drop, current density and Joule loss on saved traces, pads, filled zones and plated via barrels. The default 2.5D model and an optional Gmsh tetrahedral 3D copper-volume model have native result views and export field evidence. Independently specified current sinks support supply budgets and voltage requirements. Explicit R/L/C load-step studies, uniform-grid steady electrothermal coupling and lumped thermal-RC transient coupling are available with declared parameters and model limits. KiCad 10 native Python with NumPy, SciPy, VTK and Matplotlib is required; the 3D mode additionally needs Gmsh. These are screening models; full-wave AC and regulator current-limit control loops are not modeled. Explicit current-driven AC cross-section studies resolve skin and proximity effects in straight rectangular copper/return conductors, sum DC and harmonic RMS Joule losses, and report mesh/air-boundary sensitivity. Native and CLI workflows include waveform helpers and HTML/JSON evidence. This does not infer whole-board AC geometry or simulate a complete nonlinear converter, dielectric breakdown or HV insulation. Explicit individual C/ESR/ESL banks and finite-rise prescribed current ramps are supported in standalone lumped transients, with branch traces, conservation and half-step evidence. Reviewed same-component/net current-terminal groups retain one total current and explicit R/RL/drop models. An editable power-intent tree preserves signed rails and isolation without inferring conductive device models. Post-multi-net planar spacing screening uses explicit applicable rules and voltage references; physical creepage needs reviewed surface evidence and is not certified. A source-backed editable thermal material library supports electrothermal setup.
